moduleTitle: Module 1. Foundations, Membranes and Cell Signaling

competencies.name: Physiology and levels of function
competencies.can: Define physiology and place a given process at the correct level of organization from molecule to organism, then state the level at which that process is best explained.

competencies.name: Structure and function relationship
competencies.can: Predict how a change in the structure of a molecule, cell, tissue, or organ alters its function, using examples from two different organ systems.

competencies.name: Homeostasis defined
competencies.can: Define homeostasis, regulated variable, and setpoint, and distinguish homeostasis from chemical equilibrium and from steady state.

competencies.name: Feedback loop components
competencies.can: Diagram a negative feedback loop labeling stimulus, sensor, afferent path, integrating center, efferent path, effector, and response, and trace body temperature or blood glucose through every step.

competencies.name: Negative and positive feedback
competencies.can: Distinguish negative from positive feedback by the direction of the response and give a physiological example of each, explaining why a positive feedback loop needs an outside event to end it.

competencies.name: Feedforward control and acclimatization
competencies.can: Explain anticipatory feedforward control and acclimatization and identify which one is operating in a given scenario.

competencies.name: Local and reflex control pathways
competencies.can: Distinguish a local control pathway from a long distance reflex pathway and classify a given response as one or the other.

competencies.name: Mass balance
competencies.can: Apply the mass balance equation to a solute or to body water and calculate the intake, production, and output combination that holds the amount in the body constant.

competencies.name: Body fluid compartments
competencies.can: State the approximate volumes of total body water, intracellular fluid, extracellular fluid, plasma, and interstitial fluid in a 70 kg adult and compare the dominant solutes of the intracellular and extracellular compartments.

competencies.name: Compartment separation and clinical volume shifts
competencies.can: Predict the direction of water movement between compartments when extracellular osmolarity rises or falls and name a clinical situation that produces each shift.
